references.title: Follow one ray all the way to one pixel.
references.paper: NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields for View Synthesis
references.look: Track the same rays through sampling, density and color, volume rendering, and the final pixel residual.
references.mechanism: A learned field supplies density and view-dependent color; volume rendering accumulates these along camera rays.
references.construction: Carry identifiable rays from a 3D scene into depth profiles and finally into pixel-color comparisons.
references.eye: A pixel is an accumulation through space—not a color emitted by an unexplained network box.
references.stronger: A pipeline names the stages. Following the ray exposes the physical meaning of the intermediate quantities.
references.borrow: Choose one traceable object and preserve its identity across every change of representation.
references.limit: This explains image formation and optimization. It does not imply that reconstructed scene geometry is unique.

transfer.move: Keep one trace through every representation
transfer.when: A physical or computational signal passes through several representations before producing an observation.
trace: Choose one camera ray in a.
Follow its sampled locations into color and density in b, then the depth profile in c.
Find the corresponding pixel comparison in d: the chain ends in an observable residual.
transfer.map: Ray → your traceable query; samples → local states; accumulation → actual reduction; pixel → observable output.
transfer.keep: Retain one trace identity through every panel, even when the representation changes.
build: Pick one representative query and reveal its inputs in context.
Carry its intermediate quantities into the actual aggregation.
Attach the output and measured residual at the end of the same trace.
transfer.check: Can every stage's output be matched to the next stage's input? Verify the actual reduction, units and weighting.
transfer.example: For transport, trace one inlet packet through local interactions into a measured outlet response.
transfer.avoid: A pipeline of named boxes does not show what is being transformed.

references.label: MEGA-plate evolution
references.title: An evolutionary tree grows inside its obstacle course.
references.paper: Spatiotemporal microbial evolution on antibiotic landscapes
references.evidence: Observed colony landscape + inferred ancestry overlay
references.look: Move inward from either edge through the antibiotic bands; follow the branching lineages on the actual plate.
references.mechanism: Adaptation unfolds while expanding populations encounter successively stronger antibiotic barriers.
references.construction: Place the ancestry tree directly on the physical growth landscape, with resistance measurements and concentration bands.
references.eye: Evolution has a route through space: branching and advancement occur in a structured environment, not in an abstract tree.
references.stronger: A resistance-versus-time curve removes the geography. A detached tree removes the selective obstacles.
references.borrow: When history depends on an environment, embed the history in that environment rather than placing it in a separate panel.
references.limit: The photograph is observed; ancestry connections are inferred from video. Resistance measurements and environmental concentration are distinct quantities.

transfer.move: Place history inside its environment
transfer.when: Branching, adaptation or movement depends on spatially organized obstacles or resources.
trace: Read the antibiotic bands from the outside toward the center.
Follow a lineage as the colony expands and branches across those bands.
Keep the ancestry overlay and the photographed growth landscape in view together.
transfer.map: Plate → your environment; concentration band → barrier; lineage → inferred history; colony image → observed state.
transfer.keep: Do not detach the path from its physical coordinates. Mark inferred ancestry separately from direct observation.
build: Use the environment as the base layer.
Place events and trajectories at their actual locations and stages.
Attach the relevant local measurements without replacing the environmental context.
transfer.check: Can the reader explain where progression stalled and where it advanced? Validate event ordering and ancestry separately.
transfer.example: For adaptive exploration, overlay the verified search trajectory and branch points on the actual obstacle or reward landscape.
transfer.avoid: A shortest path drawn after the fact is not an observed history.

references.commentary_origin: MechanismFigures design interpretation; not a quotation or endorsement by the paper authors.

references.label: Multisample Flow Matching
references.title: Show when structure forms—and what a coarse solver misses.
references.paper: Multisample Flow Matching: Straightening Flows with Minibatch Couplings
references.look: Read each density sequence left to right; then inspect its low-evaluation solver outputs on the right.
references.mechanism: The coupling changes the intermediate probability path and how well a coarse numerical solver reaches the target.
references.construction: Align whole density evolutions across methods. Attach matched low-budget outputs to the same rows.
references.eye: Some paths acquire checkerboard structure early; others leave difficult rearrangement until late.
references.stronger: An endpoint score hides when the work happens. The sequence ties intermediate structure to a visible computational consequence.
references.borrow: If timing explains an outcome, align intermediate states and place the budget-limited consequence immediately beside them.
references.limit: These are density snapshots, not individual trajectories. The 2D example does not establish universal low-step performance.

transfer.move: Put the intermediate work beside its computational cost
transfer.when: Methods reach similar endpoints through different intermediate states or demand different solver budgets.
trace: Read density evolution from left to right using the common time columns.
Compare when the checkerboard structure begins forming in different rows.
Move to the right-hand solver outputs: inspect what survives at a small number of function evaluations.
transfer.map: Density → your evolving state distribution; time columns → matched stages; solver columns → matched compute budgets.
transfer.keep: Use consistent time, domain and display scale across methods. Do not confuse distribution snapshots with particle trajectories.
build: Align a small set of informative intermediate stages across methods.
Place the budget-limited output beside each corresponding evolution.
Connect the observed difference to a measured numerical or computational consequence.
transfer.check: Is the claimed mechanism visible before the endpoint? Match compute and inspect whether the intermediate difference predicts the result.
transfer.example: For iterative reconstruction, align intermediate reconstructions and show the result when every method is stopped at the same budget.
transfer.avoid: Do not choose different favorable timesteps for different methods.

references.commentary_origin: MechanismFigures design interpretation; not a quotation or endorsement by the paper authors.

references.label: Functionally invariant paths
references.title: Many parameter locations, nearly the same function.
references.paper: Engineering flexible machine learning systems by traversing functionally invariant paths
references.look: Compare the separated weight-space locations with the tightly grouped task outputs at the right.
references.mechanism: Parameters may change substantially while task behavior is approximately preserved, allowing other properties to be adjusted.
references.construction: Separate weight space from output space. Show an extended set in one mapping to a compact set in the other.
references.eye: Movement in parameters need not mean comparable movement in behavior.
references.stronger: An accuracy curve reports preservation. The paired spaces explain which freedom preservation can leave available.
references.borrow: For an invariance claim, show both the space where change occurs and the space where change must remain small.
references.limit: The surface is schematic, not a measured 3D manifold or proof of exact global functional invariance.

transfer.move: Separate the space that changes from the space that stays fixed
transfer.when: Large internal changes can preserve a specified external behavior.
trace: Find the different parameter points on the weight-space surface.
Follow their relationship to the compact group in output space.
Notice the contrast: internal movement and task-output movement have different magnitudes.
transfer.map: Weights → your internal state; surface → feasible behavior-preserving set; output cluster → the specified invariance criterion.
transfer.keep: Define the preserved behavior and tolerance. Do not present conceptual surface geometry as measured structure.
build: Draw the changing representation and the preserved representation in separate aligned spaces.
Connect corresponding states between the spaces.
Show the size of allowed output change using actual measurements where available.
transfer.check: Is preservation verified on the intended inputs, not just one illustrated example? Label approximate versus exact invariance.
transfer.example: For compression, show substantially different model encodings mapping to matched outputs on the held-out evaluation set.
transfer.avoid: Equal task accuracy is not identical function behavior on every input.

references.commentary_origin: MechanismFigures design interpretation; not a quotation or endorsement by the paper authors.

references.label: GNNExplainer
references.title: Subtract the irrelevant routes without moving the graph.
references.paper: GNNExplainer: Generating Explanations for Graph Neural Networks
references.look: Keep the red target node fixed. Watch message routes disappear and feature entries get crossed out.
references.mechanism: An explanation selects graph structure and node-feature information relevant to a model's prediction.
references.construction: Repeat the same graph layout. Retain the explanatory routes; hollow out other nodes and mask feature dimensions.
references.eye: The proposed explanation is a specific pathway through a specific neighborhood—not a list of important variables.
references.stronger: A feature ranking discards connectivity. Fixed-layout subtraction exposes both relational and feature selection.
references.borrow: To explain selection, preserve the original world and visibly remove what the explanation excludes.
references.limit: This schematic illustrates a learned explanation. Relevance masks are not automatically causal interventions or ground-truth mechanisms.

transfer.move: Subtract routes without changing the world
transfer.when: An explanation selects dependencies or features from a larger relational structure.
trace: Locate the red target node in both panels.
Compare the same neighborhood with and without highlighted message routes.
Inspect the crossed-out feature entries: the explanation selects information as well as edges.
transfer.map: Target node → prediction of interest; edges → allowable dependencies; mask → proposed explanatory subset.
transfer.keep: Fix graph positions and target identity before and after selection. Distinguish selected importance from established causality.
build: Render the original relational structure with its target clearly identified.
Repeat that structure without re-layout.
Remove or mute the excluded routes and feature entries, retaining enough context to compare.
transfer.check: Can the reader trace the retained pathway? Test prediction fidelity and any causal claim separately.
transfer.example: For a dependency audit, keep a fixed software-call graph and reveal the subset actually exercised by one failure.
transfer.avoid: Re-layout after filtering makes selection look like structural change.

references.commentary_origin: MechanismFigures design interpretation; not a quotation or endorsement by the paper authors.

references.label: TopoMap
references.title: Flatten the data without changing which pieces merge first.
references.paper: TopoMap: A 0-dimensional Homology Preserving Projection of High-Dimensional Data
references.look: Follow the same colored components as they rotate and move; inspect the controlled gap before each merge.
references.mechanism: The projection preserves the connected-component merge structure associated with increasing distance thresholds.
references.construction: Move whole components while controlling the next joining distance. The alternate figure makes thresholds into growing balls.
references.eye: Placement is constrained by the next merge event, not chosen merely to make an appealing cluster map.
references.stronger: A finished embedding hides what it preserves. Showing its construction makes the invariant inspectable.
references.borrow: For a preservation claim, show the transformations allowed by the invariant—and the precise event they must not change.
references.limit: The guarantee concerns 0-dimensional persistence: connected components. It does not preserve all distances, loops, or higher-dimensional topology.

transfer.move: Show construction under an invariant
transfer.when: An algorithm transforms a representation while preserving a precisely defined structure.
trace: Track the colored components as complete groups, not independent points.
Watch the groups rotate and translate before the next connection.
In the related ball-growth view, see that each joining event occurs at a particular distance threshold.
transfer.map: Component → your preserved group; merge event → invariant relation; placement → allowed transformation; gap → constraint.
transfer.keep: Define the invariant narrowly: this example concerns connected-component persistence, not all topology or distances.
build: Show the pre-transformation objects with stable identity.
Depict each allowed move and the condition it must preserve.
Expose the next critical event so the reader can inspect why the move remains valid.
transfer.check: Can each step be checked against the invariant? Compute the preserved quantity before and after, including edge cases.
transfer.example: For constrained optimization, show feasible moves and the constraint boundary that prevents an invalid shortcut.
transfer.avoid: A visually similar endpoint is not proof of invariant preservation.
